items.stem: A robot continuously streams laser-scan data to a mapping node. Which ROS communication pattern fits best?

options.text: A topic with publish/subscribe, because the data is a continuous stream
options.rationale: Correct: continuous, many-to-many streaming data is a natural fit for topics.

options.text: A service, because every scan needs an immediate reply
options.rationale: Services are request/response; continuous streams do not fit that pattern well.

options.text: A parameter, because the scan is configuration
options.rationale: Scan data is runtime data, not static configuration.

options.text: A launch file, because launch files carry data
options.rationale: Launch files start nodes; they do not stream data.

items.explanation: Correct: continuous, many-to-many streaming data is a natural fit for topics.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about ROS communication are accurate? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Nodes exchange typed messages over named topics
options.rationale: Correct: topics carry typed messages between publishing and subscribing nodes.

options.text: Actions suit long-running goals that report feedback and can be cancelled
options.rationale: Correct: actions are designed for long tasks with feedback and preemption.

options.text: A service is ideal for a never-ending sensor stream
options.rationale: Services are request/response, not suited to continuous streams.

options.text: Topics guarantee a direct reply to every message
options.rationale: Publish/subscribe has no built-in reply; use services for that.

items.explanation: Correct: topics carry typed messages between publishing and subscribing nodes.

items.stem: What does ROS primarily provide to a robotics project?

options.text: A middleware and tooling layer that lets independent modules communicate and be reused
options.rationale: Correct: ROS standardises inter-process communication and tooling so components compose.

options.text: A replacement for the computer's operating system kernel
options.rationale: ROS runs on top of an OS such as Linux; it is not a kernel.

options.text: A guarantee that any robot hardware will work without drivers
options.rationale: Hardware still needs drivers; ROS does not remove that need.

options.text: A single monolithic program that controls the whole robot
options.rationale: ROS encourages many small nodes, not one monolith.

items.explanation: Correct: ROS standardises inter-process communication and tooling so components compose.
